To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of medications for other diseases (comorbidities) and physical functioning (PF scale) may be important parameters to assess asthma control in elderly patients.
the number of medications for the comorbidity and the physical functioning scale are significant predictors for asthma control in the elderly.
the number of medications for co-morbidities and the performance status determined by physical functioning scale may be important predictors for assessing asthma control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the predictors of asthma in elderly asthmatics.
the factors that affect the asthma control and the asthma-specific quality of Life in the elderly asthmatic population.
the predictors of asthma exacerbation and asthma-specific quality of Life (QOL) in elderly patients with asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the number of medications for other comorbidities, and the physical functioning (PF)-scale determined by the SF-36 questionnaire were important parameters for assessing the asthma control in elderly asthma patients.
the number of medications for other diseases (comorbidities) and the physical function scale were important parameters for asthma control in elderly patients.

the number of medications for other comorbidities, physical functioning, and asthma control test score at baseline were significant determinants for predicting asthma control and asthma-specific quality of the life in elderly asthmatics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the number of medications for co-morbidities and the performance status determined by PF scale may be an important parameter for assessing asthma control and the factors that determine the changes in asthma-specific quality of live in elderly asthmatics.
the number of medications for the comorbidities, performance status determined by PF scale, and ACT score at baseline were important parameters for assessing the asthma control in elderly patients.
the number of medications for co-morbidities and physical functioning were significant predictors of asthma control in the elderly asthmatic population.

the number of medications for other comorbidities, and the physical functioning scale of the EuroQOL-5D may be important parameters to assess asthma control in elderly patients.
